messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable Swordigo-inspired 2D mobile/tablet adventure game.
- Update its story to follow the boy who opens a forest door, is transported to another world, learns of a prophecy, and must collect five keys from five nations to return home.

## Requirements
- User requested a playable game for phones/tablets, then specified the story premise and key-collection goal.
- Do not copy Swordigo’s characters or assets; the existing game uses original branding and artwork.

## Decisions
- Implemented the game as a self-contained HTML canvas game in `index.html`.
- Expressed the new story through the opening text and the ending reached at the current level’s gate; five nations/keys are described as the larger quest.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built a side-scrolling game with movement, jumping, sword combat, enemies, coins, checkpoints, health, pause/restart, and mobile touch controls.
- Updated the opening story and gate ending to mention the other world, the girl, the king, the prophecy, five nations, bosses, and five keys.
- JavaScript syntax checked successfully; browser loaded the page without console errors.

### Active
- The requested full five-nation/five-key adventure is not implemented as gameplay; only the story setup and ending narration describe it.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. If continuing the feature, implement playable progression through five nations, boss encounters, key collection, and a portal-home conclusion.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Complete game implementation and updated story text.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Browser screenshot saved at `/tmp/opencode/emberfall-story.jpg`.

## Objective
- Build a playable Swordigo-inspired 2D mobile/tablet adventure game.
- Tell the story of a boy transported from a forest into another world, where he must collect five keys from five nations to open a portal home.

## Requirements
- Keep the game playable on phones and tablets.
- Use original characters and assets rather than copying Swordigo.

## Decisions
- The game is implemented as a self-contained HTML canvas game in `index.html`.
- Five regions are named Verdant Reach, Frostveil Peaks, Sunken Coast, Ashen March, and Starfall Crown; each has a guardian and a key.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented five-region progression with guardians, key collection, gates, region-specific palettes, and a portal-home ending.
- Added the prophecy and origin story to the opening text and a five-key HUD and region quest text.
- JavaScript syntax checked; page reloaded and started in the browser with no console errors.

### Active
- Validate complete gameplay progression, including guardian fights, gates, checkpoints, and the final ending; only initial browser play was tested.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test the five-region gameplay loop and fix any progression or combat issues found.
2. Check mobile/tablet layout and controls after the HUD additions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Self-contained game, story, rendering, controls, and progression implementation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Latest change standardizes each region’s second checkpoint y-coordinate to `430`.
- Browser screenshot: `/tmp/opencode/emberfall-five-nations.png`.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page
  show                        show playwright dashboard
  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions
  close-all                   close all browser sessions
  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

Global options:
  --help [command]            print help
  --json                      output response as JSON
  --raw                       output only the result value, without status and code
  --version                   print version

## Objective
- Build a playable Swordigo-inspired 2D mobile/tablet adventure about a boy transported from a forest into another world, collecting five keys from five nations to open a portal home.

## Requirements
- Keep the game playable on phones and tablets.
- Use original characters and assets rather than copying Swordigo.

## Decisions
- Implement the game as a self-contained HTML canvas game in `index.html`.
- Five regions: Verdant Reach, Frostveil Peaks, Sunken Coast, Ashen March, and Starfall Crown; each has a guardian and a key.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented five-region progression, guardian fights, keys, gates, region palettes, prophecy/origin story, HUD, quest text, and portal-home ending.
- Added death recovery at the last checkpoint and barriers at locked nation gates.
- Made sword attack repeat while held, so players can land successive hits without tapping for every strike.
- Adjusted the mobile HUD at widths up to 540px: status panel sits below the brand and quest text below both.
- JavaScript syntax checked; Playwright confirmed the initial mobile layout has no brand/status overlap and that movement collects coins.

### Active
- Validate complete gameplay progression and fix any combat, movement, checkpoint, or gate issues found.
- Verify that death recovery and checkpoint placement work as intended.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Investigate remaining combat/progression issues: recent simulated play did not defeat Mossfang, and the player repeatedly reached the death screen.
2. Re-test boss fights, gate transitions, checkpoint recovery, ending, and mobile controls after fixing gameplay issues.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Self-contained game source, story, rendering, controls, HUD, and progression.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed `index.html` and other untracked project files.
- `hurt(true)` now respawns at the platform floor matching the checkpoint’s x-coordinate rather than always using the world ground.
- At 390×844, `.brand` occupies y=12–43, `.status` y=52–96, and `.quest` y=104–143.
- Simulated gameplay collected three coins without losing health but did not advance to the guardian; a separate movement-plus-attack simulation ended at “Not the end.”

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a playable Swordigo-inspired 2D mobile/tablet adventure about a boy transported from a forest into another world, collecting five keys from five nations to open a portal home.

## Requirements
- Keep the game playable on phones and tablets.
- Use original characters and assets rather than copying Swordigo.

## Decisions
- Implement the game as a self-contained HTML canvas game in `index.html`.
- Five regions: Verdant Reach, Frostveil Peaks, Sunken Coast, Ashen March, and Starfall Crown; each has a guardian and a key.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented five-region progression, guardian fights, keys, gates, region palettes, story, HUD, quest text, and portal-home ending.
- Added death recovery at the last checkpoint and barriers at locked nation gates.
- Made sword attacks repeat while held.
- Adjusted the mobile HUD layout for narrow screens.
- Identified gaps between platforms that caused falls; extended a platform across one gap and increased starting health from 3 to 5.
- Reduced common enemies to one hit and broadened their attack proximity.
- JavaScript syntax checked successfully after changes.

### Active
- Validate complete gameplay progression; guardian combat has not yet been demonstrated to work, and recent simulations lost health before reaching Mossfang.
- Continue tuning combat reach and damage feedback, then verify all region gates, checkpoints, death recovery, ending, and mobile controls.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect and fix the guardian hit detection and attack timing; the latest change increased the sword animation’s progress denominator from `.24` to `.36`, but gameplay remains unverified.
2. Remove temporary `window.__debug` instrumentation from `index.html` when testing is complete.
3. Re-test long-form progression and mobile HUD/controls.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Self-contained game source, story, rendering, controls, HUD, and progression.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files were previously listed as untracked.
- Playwright simulations showed the player can reach later sections but still loses health and has not reached or defeated the first guardian.
- `basePlatforms` now extends the platform at `x:790` from width `360` to `620`; player starts with 5 HP; common enemies have 1 HP and a wider hit radius.
- Temporary `window.__debug` exposes player, boss, coin, and screen state for browser tests.

## Objective
- Build a playable Swordigo-inspired adventure in `index.html`, then change its gameplay to a true isometric angle.

## Requirements
- Playable on phones and tablets.
- Use original characters and assets rather than copying Swordigo.
- The player chose true isometric gameplay: move in four directions across angled ground, adapting platforms, enemies, and camera.

## Decisions
- The game is a self-contained HTML canvas game.
- The story spans five regions, each with a guardian and key; collecting all five opens the portal home.
- Replace vertical platforming with true isometric movement, rather than only tilting the visuals.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented five-region progression, guardian fights, keys, gates, region palettes, story, HUD, checkpoints, death recovery, and portal-home ending.
- Improved sword combat timing and damage feedback; browser simulation confirmed all five guardians can be defeated and the ending reached.
- Added jump buffering/coyote-time logic, increased player health, and tuned common enemy health and reach.
- JavaScript syntax checked successfully.

### Active
- Convert the existing 2D platform game into true isometric gameplay and update mobile controls accordingly.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Refactor movement and world coordinates from horizontal platforming to four-direction isometric movement.
2. Adapt terrain, collision, enemies, guardians, gates, camera, rendering, and controls for the isometric world.
3. Re-test full progression, ending, and mobile/tablet playability.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Self-contained game source and the primary file to update.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files were previously untracked.
- `index.html` still contains the original platformer, including temporary `window.__debug` instrumentation that should be removed after testing.
- Current touch controls are left/right, attack, and jump; keyboard controls are left/right, jump, and attack.

## Requirements

- Address its language/framework, rendering engine, 3D capabilities, models/animation/shadows/collision, mobile controls, eight-direction movement, and safest upgrade or migration strategy.

- Identified the current game as a single-file HTML/CSS/JavaScript game using Canvas 2D and custom game logic, not Phaser, Three.js, Babylon.js, or another 3D engine.

1. Explain that Canvas 2D can simulate an isometric look but does not provide genuine 3D rendering or built-in 3D character rigs, skeletal animation, 3D shadows, or 3D collision.
2. Recommend a migration path—likely Three.js for a browser-based project—with an orthographic camera, 3D scene/assets, animation and collision systems, and retained HTML HUD/mobile controls.
3. Propose staged implementation that keeps the current game as a working baseline and ports gameplay systems incrementally; make no file changes.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire current game implementation, including Canvas 2D rendering, gameplay, UI, and touch controls.
- `README.md`: Project description; identifies the project as created with OMGithub.

content.text:
## Technical assessment

1. **Language and framework:** The game is written in HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript. It is currently a self-contained browser game rather than a project built around a game framework.

2. **Rendering engine:** It uses **HTML Canvas 2D** and custom game logic. There is no current use of Phaser, Three.js, Babylon.js, or another 3D engine.

3. **Genuine 3D and an isometric camera:** Canvas 2D can draw an isometric-looking scene, but it does not provide a genuine 3D scene or camera. A 3D engine such as **Three.js** can render actual 3D geometry with an orthographic camera positioned at an isometric angle.

4. **Models, animation, shadows, and collision:** These are all feasible after adding a 3D engine. Three.js can load 3D character and environment assets, including skeletal animations in formats such as glTF/GLB. Shadows and 3D collision are also possible, but they require implementation and performance tuning; they are not features the current Canvas renderer provides. A physics library such as Rapier could handle collision and movement, or a smaller custom system could suit a simpler game.

5. **Current mobile controls:** The game uses HTML buttons and Pointer Events for directional movement and attacking. It has a four-button directional pad, not an analog joystick.

6. **Eight-direction movement:** The existing movement combines horizontal and vertical input and normalizes diagonal movement. That already allows movement in eight directions, but it is **digital**—players press combinations of discrete buttons rather than steering smoothly. For analog movement, replace or supplement the directional pad with a touch joystick that tracks pointer position and applies a dead zone and normalized input. In the 3D version, movement should also be mapped consistently to the camera’s ground plane.

## Recommended migration plan

The safest path is to preserve the existing game as a working reference and introduce Three.js incrementally, rather than trying to convert the Canvas renderer in place all at once:

1. **Preserve a runnable baseline.** Keep the current game intact while establishing a separate 3D entry point or branch of the implementation. Avoid removing current controls, UI, or gameplay until their replacements work.
2. **Set up the 3D foundation.** Add a Three.js scene, renderer, isometric orthographic camera, resize handling, and a simple test environment. Confirm this runs in the project’s existing deployment setup before committing to a larger build-system change.
3. **Port gameplay in stages.** Bring over movement and camera follow first, then collision and level geometry, combat and enemies, and finally progression and other game systems. Keep the existing HTML HUD and touch controls where practical.
4. **Add assets and animation.** Integrate 3D character and environment models, then connect animation states to gameplay actions. Add lighting and shadows with mobile performance in mind.
5. **Verify and retire deliberately.** Test desktop and mobile controls, movement in all directions, collisions, and performance. Keep the 2D version available until the 3D game reaches feature parity or you explicitly decide to replace it.

**Bottom line:** The current game does not provide genuine 3D itself, but the browser project can be upgraded to do so. Three.js is a practical fit for a browser-based 3D game with an orthographic isometric view. The existing controls and gameplay can be retained as a baseline while the 3D version is built and validated.

No files have been modified or deleted.

## Objective
- Upgrade the existing Swordigo-inspired game into a polished genuine 3D isometric action-adventure RPG using Three.js while preserving the original project and working features.

## Requirements
- Preserve the original project and make a backup before major changes.
- Use an orthographic isometric camera, approximately 45° horizontal rotation and 35° downward elevation.
- Support camera-relative eight-direction movement, smooth acceleration/deceleration, camera follow, solid-obstacle collision, and natural Android touch controls.
- Prioritize clean, functional code and mobile performance.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js for genuine 3D rendering.
- Keep the existing HTML HUD and gameplay structure where practical; retain the original game as a backup/reference.
- Integrate Three.js as an ES module with an import map to `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.180.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Replace the mobile D-pad with an analog joystick while retaining the attack control.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html.backup` as a snapshot of the original game.
- Added a Three.js implementation in `game.js` with scene, camera, environment, gameplay, keyboard input, collision, camera-relative movement, and UI integration.
- Updated `index.html` to load `game.js` as a module and provide a mobile joystick and attack control.
- Added joystick pointer handling, keyboard controls, pointer-based attack input, and input release handling.
- Served and opened the game in Playwright at `http://localhost:3002`; title screen and gameplay rendered, and starting the game worked.
- `node --check game.js` passed; browser reported zero console errors.

### Active
- Validate runtime behavior, gameplay, camera framing, collisions, and mobile performance.

### Blocked
- Browser emitted WebGL performance/feedback-loop warnings during screenshot capture; their impact and whether they indicate an issue remain unverified.

## Next Move
1. Inspect gameplay and title screenshots; verify the scene framing and rendering.
2. Test desktop keyboard gameplay, collisions, combat, and camera follow.
3. Test mobile joystick and attack, including pointer cancellation and simultaneous touches.
4. Investigate the WebGL warnings and address any functional or performance problems.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entry point, HUD, mobile controls, and Three.js module loading.
- `game.js`: Three.js implementation and gameplay/input logic.
- `index.html.backup`: Original game snapshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- The previous Canvas 2D game was replaced at the entry point; its original snapshot remains in `index.html.backup`.
- Playwright showed WebGL2; no console errors were reported, but screenshot capture produced five WebGL warnings.

- Use an orthographic isometric camera, approximately 45° horizontal rotation and 35° downward elevation.
- Support camera-relative eight-direction movement, smooth acceleration/deceleration, camera follow, solid-obstacle collision, and natural Android touch controls.

## Objective
- Upgrade the existing Swordigo-inspired game into a polished genuine 3D isometric action-adventure RPG using Three.js while preserving the original project and working features.

## Requirements
- Preserve the original project and make a backup before major changes.
- Use an orthographic isometric camera, approximately 45° horizontal rotation and 35° downward elevation.
- Support camera-relative eight-direction movement, smooth acceleration/deceleration, camera follow, solid-obstacle collision, and natural Android touch controls.
- Prioritize clean, functional code and mobile performance.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js as an ES module from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.180.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Keep the existing HTML HUD and gameplay structure where practical; retain the original game as a backup/reference.
- Replace the mobile D-pad with an analog joystick while retaining the attack control.

## Work State
### Completed
- Backed up the original game as `index.html.backup`.
- Implemented the Three.js scene, environment, gameplay, keyboard input, collision, camera-relative movement, camera follow, and UI integration in `game.js`.
- Updated `index.html` for module loading, mobile joystick, and attack controls.
- Added joystick pointer handling, keyboard controls, pointer-based attacks, and input release handling.
- Adjusted portrait mobile camera framing to use a 16-unit view height in `game.js`.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Browser checks confirmed gameplay starts, desktop movement input leaves the game running with full health, and Escape pause/resume works.
- Confirmed mobile controls fit within the 390×844 viewport.
- Clean reload and start produced no console warnings; no JavaScript errors observed.
- Captured screenshots including `/tmp/opencode/emberfall-mobile-input-test.png`.

### Active
- Validate actual joystick and attack pointer interactions, combat, obstacle collision, and camera follow.
- Assess the occasional WebGL warning during pointer/drag testing.

### Blocked
- Browser drag testing does not establish reliable real multitouch/joystick behavior; touch interaction and simultaneous movement/attack remain unverified.

## Next Move
1. Test joystick movement, pointer cancellation/release, and simultaneous joystick-plus-attack input with appropriate touch events or a real mobile device.
2. Verify combat hits, obstacle collision, and camera follow in gameplay.
3. Investigate whether `GL_INVALID_OPERATION: glBlitFramebuffer: Blit feedback loop: the read and draw framebuffers are the same.` recurs during ordinary play; it appeared once during mobile drag testing but not on clean reload/start.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js implementation, gameplay, input, and portrait camera framing.
- `index.html`: Entry point, HUD, mobile controls, and Three.js module loading.
- `index.html.backup`: Original game snapshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `git status --short`.
- Desktop keyboard checks used synthetic browser `KeyboardEvent`s; mobile drag testing reset the joystick afterward but did not prove movement or multitouch behavior.
- Earlier screenshot captures showed `GPU stall due to ReadPixels` and `GL_INVALID_OPERATION: glBlitFramebuffer: Blit feedback loop`; recent clean reload/start had no warnings, while one drag test reproduced the blit warning.

## Objective
- Upgrade the existing Swordigo-inspired game into a polished genuine 3D isometric action-adventure RPG using Three.js while preserving the original project and working features.

## Requirements
- Preserve the original project and make a backup before major changes.
- Use an orthographic isometric camera, approximately 45° horizontal rotation and 35° downward elevation.
- Support camera-relative eight-direction movement, smooth acceleration/deceleration, camera follow, solid-obstacle collision, and natural Android touch controls.
- Prioritize clean, functional code and mobile performance.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js as an ES module from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.180.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Keep the existing HTML HUD and gameplay structure where practical; retain the original game as a backup/reference.
- Replace the mobile D-pad with an analog joystick while retaining the attack control.

## Work State
### Completed
- Backed up the original game as `index.html.backup`.
- Implemented the Three.js scene, environment, gameplay, keyboard input, collision, camera-relative movement, camera follow, and UI integration in `game.js`.
- Updated `index.html` for module loading, mobile joystick, and attack controls.
- Added joystick pointer handling, keyboard controls, pointer-based attacks, and input release handling.
- Adjusted portrait mobile camera framing to use a 16-unit view height in `game.js`.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Browser checks confirmed gameplay starts, desktop movement input leaves the game running with full health, and Escape pause/resume works.
- Confirmed mobile controls fit within the 390×844 viewport.
- CDP touch-event testing confirmed joystick movement, simultaneous joystick-plus-attack input, separate release of joystick while attack remains pressed, and final input release/reset.
- Clean reload and start produced no console warnings; no JavaScript errors observed.
- Captured screenshots including `/tmp/opencode/emberfall-mobile-input-test.png`.

### Active
- Validate combat hits, obstacle collision, and camera follow in gameplay.
- Investigate the intermittent WebGL blit feedback-loop warning.

### Blocked
- No real Android device test has been performed; browser touch emulation confirms simultaneous controls but not device-specific behavior.

## Next Move
1. Verify combat hits, obstacle collision, and camera follow during gameplay.
2. Check whether `GL_INVALID_OPERATION: glBlitFramebuffer: Blit feedback loop: the read and draw framebuffers are the same.` recurs during ordinary play and investigate if needed.
3. If possible, test joystick and simultaneous movement/attack on a real Android device.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js implementation, gameplay, input, collision, and camera framing.
- `index.html`: Entry point, HUD, mobile controls, and Three.js module loading.
- `index.html.backup`: Original game snapshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `git status --short`.
- Desktop keyboard checks used synthetic browser `KeyboardEvent`s.
- CDP touch emulation verified joystick travel (computed knob transform `matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, 32, 0)`) and simultaneous attack; all controls reset on release.
- The WebGL warning did not appear on clean reload/start, but recurred during touch-event testing.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page
  show                        show playwright dashboard
  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions
  close-all                   close all browser sessions
  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

Global options:
  --help [command]            print help
  --json                      output response as JSON

  --version                   print version

## Objective
- Upgrade the existing Swordigo-inspired game into a polished genuine 3D isometric action-adventure RPG using Three.js while preserving the original project and working features.

## Requirements
- Preserve the original project and make a backup before major changes.
- Use an orthographic isometric camera, approximately 45° horizontal rotation and 35° downward elevation.
- Support camera-relative eight-direction movement, smooth acceleration/deceleration, camera follow, solid-obstacle collision, and natural Android touch controls.
- Prioritize clean, functional code and mobile performance.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js as an ES module from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.180.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Keep the existing HTML HUD and gameplay structure where practical; retain the original game as a backup/reference.
- Replace the mobile D-pad with an analog joystick while retaining the attack control.

## Work State
### Completed
- Backed up the original game as `index.html.backup`.
- Implemented the Three.js scene, environment, gameplay, keyboard input, collision, camera-relative movement, camera follow, and UI integration in `game.js`.
- Updated `index.html` for module loading, mobile joystick, and attack controls.
- Added joystick pointer handling, keyboard controls, pointer-based attacks, and input release handling.
- Adjusted portrait mobile camera framing to use a 16-unit view height in `game.js`.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Browser checks confirmed gameplay starts, Escape pause/resume works, and mobile controls fit within the 390×844 viewport.
- CDP touch tests confirmed joystick movement, simultaneous joystick-plus-attack input, separate joystick release while attack remains pressed, and final input release/reset.
- Clean reload/start and later touch checks produced no JavaScript errors or console warnings.
- Captured mobile input screenshot at `/tmp/opencode/emberfall-mobile-input-test.png`.

### Active
- Validate combat hits and solid-obstacle collision in gameplay.
- Inspect camera-follow screenshots at `/tmp/opencode/camera-before.png` and `/tmp/opencode/camera-after.png`.
- Determine whether the intermittent WebGL blit feedback-loop warning recurs during ordinary play.

### Blocked
- No real Android device test has been performed; browser touch emulation confirms simultaneous controls but not device-specific behavior.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the camera screenshots and verify the camera follows the player during movement.
2. Run focused gameplay checks for enemy/boss hits and obstacle collision; previous attack attempts did not produce conclusive results.
3. Continue observing WebGL output for `GL_INVALID_OPERATION: glBlitFramebuffer: Blit feedback loop: the read and draw framebuffers are the same.`
4. Test joystick and simultaneous movement/attack on a real Android device if possible.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js implementation, gameplay, input, collision, and camera framing.
- `index.html`: Entry point, HUD, mobile controls, and Three.js module loading.
- `index.html.backup`: Original game snapshot.

- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `git status --short`.

- The WebGL warning recurred in earlier touch-event testing but did not appear during the most recent touch check.

## Objective
- Upgrade the existing Swordigo-inspired game into a polished 3D isometric action-adventure RPG using Three.js while preserving the original project and working features.

## Requirements
- Preserve the original project and make a backup before major changes.
- Use an orthographic isometric camera, approximately 45° horizontal rotation and 35° downward elevation.
- Support camera-relative eight-direction movement, smooth acceleration/deceleration, camera follow, solid-obstacle collision, and natural Android touch controls.
- Prioritize clean, functional code and mobile performance.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js as an ES module from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.180.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Keep the existing HTML HUD and gameplay structure where practical; retain the original game as a backup/reference.
- Replace the mobile D-pad with an analog joystick while retaining the attack control.

## Work State
### Completed
- Backed up the original game as `index.html.backup`.
- Implemented the Three.js scene, environment, gameplay, keyboard input, collision, camera-relative movement, camera follow, and UI integration in `game.js`.
- Updated `index.html` for module loading, mobile joystick, and attack controls.
- Browser checks verified keyboard/touch input behavior, Escape pause/resume, and mobile control fit.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed.
- CDP touch emulation verified joystick travel, simultaneous attack, independent input release, and control reset.
- Inspected camera screenshots at `/tmp/opencode/camera-before.png` and `/tmp/opencode/camera-after.png`.

### Active
- Diagnose combat: focused tests did not confirm enemy hits; test snapshots show the hero facing diagonally while enemies remain out of strike range.
- Verify solid-obstacle collision during gameplay.
- Recheck camera follow and whether the WebGL feedback-loop warning recurs in ordinary play.

### Blocked
- Real Android device testing has not been performed; browser touch emulation does not confirm device-specific behavior.

## Next Move
1. Use controlled gameplay tests to establish enemy engagement and verify that attacks reduce enemy health; investigate reach/facing if needed.
2. Test collision against a known obstacle and inspect camera follow while moving.
3. Check whether `GL_INVALID_OPERATION: glBlitFramebuffer: Blit feedback loop: the read and draw framebuffers are the same.` recurs.
4. Remove the temporary `window.__debugGame` hook from `game.js` after debugging.
5. Test joystick and simultaneous movement/attack on a real Android device if possible.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js implementation, gameplay, input, collision, camera framing; currently includes temporary `window.__debugGame` diagnostics.
- `index.html`: Entry point, HUD, mobile controls, and Three.js module loading.
- `index.html.backup`: Original game snapshot.
- `/tmp/opencode/camera-before.png`: Camera screenshot for comparison.
- `/tmp/opencode/camera-after.png`: Camera screenshot for comparison.
- `/home/runner/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/output/console-2026-11-07T06-54-00-513Z.log`: Captured WebGL warning and unrelated favicon 404.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `git status --short`.
- Recent Playwright movement-and-attack attempts did not conclusively demonstrate combat hits; diagnostic snapshots showed the hero near `(96.34, 188.66)` facing `(0.707, -0.707)` while the nearest enemy was around `(144.91, 174.57)`.
- The WebGL blit feedback-loop warning appeared once in the captured browser log; recurrence is unverified.

- Preserve the original project and make a backup before major changes.

- Retain the original game as a backup/reference and keep the existing HTML HUD and gameplay structure where practical.
- Replace the mobile D-pad with an analog joystick while retaining the attack control.
- Let active attacks hit nearby enemies without requiring them to remain in front of the hero.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Upgrade the existing Swordigo-inspired game into a polished 3D isometric action-adventure RPG while preserving the original project and working features.
- Improve the retained hero’s procedural animation, including locomotion, turning, foot placement, attacks, and jump phases.

## Requirements
- Preserve the original project and make a backup before major changes.
- Use an orthographic isometric camera, approximately 45° horizontal rotation and 35° downward elevation.
- Support camera-relative eight-direction movement, smooth acceleration/deceleration, camera follow, solid-obstacle collision, and natural Android touch controls.
- Keep code clean and mobile performance in mind.
- Blend animations smoothly by movement speed; idle, walking, and running should look natural, and the character should face movement direction.
- Include takeoff, airborne, and landing animation phases; retain the existing character.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js as an ES module from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.180.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Retain the original game as a backup/reference and keep the existing HTML HUD and gameplay structure where practical.
- Use procedural animation because the current character has no skeletal rig.
- Replace the mobile D-pad with an analog joystick while retaining attack controls.
- Let active attacks hit nearby enemies without requiring them to remain in front of the hero.

## Work State
### Completed
- Backed up the original game as `index.html.backup`; implemented Three.js gameplay, UI integration, keyboard/touch controls, movement, collision, and camera follow.
- Browser checks verified keyboard/touch input behavior, Escape pause/resume, mobile control fit, joystick/attack input handling, combat hit registration, obstacle collision, and camera follow.
- Controlled combat test verified enemy HP reduction and defeat.
- Removed temporary `window.__debugGame` diagnostics.
- Restructured the existing hero model with torso, head, arm, and leg pivots; added feet and procedural idle, gait, turning, attack, and jump poses.
- Connected `animateHero()` to the gameplay update loop and added keyboard-space jump input plus takeoff, airborne, and landing state transitions.

### Active
- Validate the latest animation and jump changes in a browser; check animation transforms and attack compatibility.
- Decide whether to expose jump on mobile; current mobile controls still only include joystick and attack.

### Blocked
- Real Android device testing has not been performed; browser touch emulation cannot confirm device-specific behavior.

## Next Move
1. Run `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`.
2. Verify idle, movement transitions, rotation, attacks, and jump phases in a browser; resolve any pose or gameplay conflicts.
3. Consider adding a mobile jump control if touch jumping is required, then verify joystick and simultaneous movement/attack.
4. Test on a real Android device if available.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js gameplay, hero procedural animation, controls, jump state, collision, and camera follow.
- `index.html`: Entry point, HUD, mobile controls, and Three.js module loading.
- `index.html.backup`: Original game snapshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in Git.
- The latest animation/jump edits have not yet been validated.
- Jump is currently mapped to the keyboard spacebar; no mobile jump button is present, and `.control.jump` is hidden.
- A previous browser run reported `GL_INVALID_OPERATION: glBlitFramebuffer: Blit feedback loop: the read and draw framebuffers are the same.` It did not recur in later checks.

## Objective
- Upgrade the existing Swordigo-inspired game into a polished 3D isometric action-adventure RPG while preserving the original project and working features.
- Improve the retained hero’s procedural animation, including locomotion, turning, attacks, and jump phases.

## Requirements
- Preserve the original game and make a backup before major changes.
- Use an orthographic isometric camera, approximately 45° horizontal rotation and 35° downward elevation.
- Support camera-relative eight-direction movement, smooth acceleration/deceleration, camera follow, solid-obstacle collision, and natural Android touch controls.
- Keep code clean and mobile performance in mind.
- Blend animations smoothly by movement speed; idle, walking, and running should look natural, and the character should face movement direction.
- Include takeoff, airborne, and landing animation phases; retain the existing character.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js as an ES module from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.180.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Retain the original game as a backup/reference and keep the existing HTML HUD and gameplay structure where practical.
- Use procedural animation because the current character has no skeletal rig.
- Replace the mobile D-pad with an analog joystick while retaining attack controls.
- Let active attacks hit nearby enemies without requiring them to remain in front of the hero.
- Add a mobile jump button alongside keyboard Space jump.

## Work State
### Completed
- Backed up the original game as `index.html.backup`; implemented Three.js gameplay, UI integration, keyboard/touch controls, movement, collision, and camera follow.
- Browser checks verified keyboard/touch input behavior, Escape pause/resume, mobile control fit, joystick/attack handling, combat hit registration, obstacle collision, and camera follow.
- Controlled combat test verified enemy HP reduction and defeat.
- Removed temporary `window.__debugGame` diagnostics.
- Restructured the existing hero model with torso, head, arm, and leg pivots; added feet and procedural idle, gait, turning, attack, and jump poses.
- Connected `animateHero()` to gameplay updates and added keyboard-Space and mobile-button jump input with takeoff, airborne, and landing transitions.
- Enabled the mobile jump button in `index.html` and updated the controls hint to mention Space for jump.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Headless Chromium loaded the page and produced a 390×844 mobile screenshot; no clear game runtime exception was observed.

### Active
- Validate animation transforms and attack compatibility in a browser, including jump phases and simultaneous joystick/attack/jump input.
- Inspect the mobile screenshot/control layout and resolve any pose or gameplay conflicts.

### Blocked
- Real Android device testing has not been performed; browser emulation cannot confirm device-specific behavior.

## Next Move
1. Run interactive browser checks for idle, movement transitions, rotation, attacks, and takeoff/airborne/landing.
2. Check simultaneous mobile joystick, attack, and jump input; adjust layout or animation if needed.
3. Test on a real Android device if available.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js gameplay, hero procedural animation, controls, jump state, collision, and camera follow.
- `index.html`: Entry point, HUD, mobile controls, and Three.js module loading.
- `index.html.backup`: Original game snapshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in Git.
- Jump is mapped to keyboard Space and a mobile button; mobile controls now include joystick, attack, and jump.
- A previous browser run reported `GL_INVALID_OPERATION: glBlitFramebuffer: Blit feedback loop: the read and draw framebuffers are the same.` It did not recur in later checks.

## Objective
- Upgrade the existing Swordigo-inspired game into a polished 3D isometric action-adventure RPG while preserving the original game and working features.
- Improve the retained hero’s procedural animation, including locomotion, turning, attacks, and jump phases.

## Requirements
- Preserve the original game and keep a backup.
- Use an orthographic isometric camera, camera-relative eight-direction movement, smooth acceleration/deceleration, collision, camera follow, and mobile-friendly touch controls.
- Keep code clean and mindful of mobile performance.
- Blend idle, walking, and running naturally; face the movement direction.
- Include takeoff, airborne, and landing animation phases.
- Retain the existing character and add keyboard Space and mobile jump input.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js ES modules from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.180.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Keep the existing HTML HUD/gameplay structure where practical and retain the original in `index.html.backup`.
- Use procedural animation because the character has no skeletal rig.
- Use an analog mobile joystick with attack and jump controls.
- Allow active attacks to hit nearby enemies without a forward-facing restriction.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented Three.js gameplay, UI integration, keyboard/touch controls, movement, collision, and camera follow.
- Added procedural hero pivots and idle, gait, turning, attack, and jump poses; connected animation to gameplay updates.
- Improved animation with travel-distance-based gait cadence, body lean and turn anticipation, jump takeoff/airborne/descent poses, landing compression, and a wind-up/slash/follow-through attack.
- Added `attackHit` to limit each attack to one target hit without shortening the animation.
- Added mobile jump button and updated the controls hint.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed after the latest animation changes.

### Active
- Verify the latest animation changes in a browser, especially locomotion, turning, attacks, and jump transitions.
- Review final changes and validation results.

### Blocked
- Real Android device testing has not been performed; browser emulation cannot verify device-specific behavior.

## Next Move
1. Run browser interaction checks for locomotion, turning, attacks, and jump phases.
2. Recheck `node --check game.js`, `git diff --check`, and `git status`.
3. Test on Android if a device is available.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js gameplay, hero procedural animation, controls, jump state, collision, and camera follow.
- `index.html`: Entry point, HUD, mobile controls, and Three.js module loading.
- `index.html.backup`: Original game snapshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` lists project files as untracked.
- Earlier browser checks verified movement, combat, collisions, camera follow, pause/resume, mobile controls, jump phases, and simultaneous joystick/attack/jump input; they predate the latest animation adjustments.
- A previous browser run reported `GL_INVALID_OPERATION: glBlitFramebuffer: Blit feedback loop: the read and draw framebuffers are the same.` It did not recur in later checks.

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page
  show                        show playwright dashboard
  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions
  close-all                   close all browser sessions
  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

Global options:
  --help [command]            print help
  --json                      output response as JSON
  --raw                       output only the result value, without status and code
  --version                   print version

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Upgrade the existing Swordigo-inspired game into a polished 3D isometric action-adventure RPG while preserving the original game and working features.
- Improve the retained hero’s procedural locomotion, turning, attacks, and jump animation.

## Requirements
- Preserve the original game and keep a backup.
- Use an orthographic isometric camera, camera-relative eight-direction movement, smooth acceleration/deceleration, collision, camera follow, and mobile-friendly touch controls.
- Keep code clean and mindful of mobile performance.
- Blend idle, walking, and running naturally; face the movement direction.
- Include takeoff, airborne, and landing animation phases.
- Retain the existing character and add keyboard Space and mobile jump input.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js ES modules from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.180.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Keep the existing HTML HUD/gameplay structure where practical and retain the original in `index.html.backup`.
- Use procedural animation because the character has no skeletal rig.
- Use an analog mobile joystick with attack and jump controls.
- Allow active attacks to hit nearby enemies without a forward-facing restriction; limit each attack to one target without shortening its animation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented Three.js gameplay, UI integration, keyboard/touch controls, movement, collision, and camera follow.
- Added procedural hero pivots and idle, gait, turning, attack, and jump poses; connected animation to gameplay updates.
- Improved locomotion cadence based on travel distance, body lean and turn anticipation, takeoff/airborne/descent poses, landing compression, and attack wind-up/slash/follow-through.
- Added `attackHit` to prevent repeat hits during one attack; added mobile jump input and updated the controls hint.
- Latest `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Browser loaded the game at `http://localhost:3002/`; snapshot showed the HUD, title overlay, and controls hint. WebGL2 context was available, with no console errors.

### Active
- Verify locomotion, turning, attacks, jump transitions, and mobile controls through browser interaction checks.
- Review final changes and validation results.

### Blocked
- Real Android device testing has not been performed; browser emulation cannot verify device-specific behavior.

## Next Move
1. Run browser interaction checks for movement, turning, attack animation/hit behavior, jump phases, and touch controls.
2. Recheck `node --check game.js`, `git diff --check`, and `git status`.
3. Test on Android if a device is available.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js gameplay, procedural hero animation, controls, jump state, collision, and camera follow.
- `index.html`: Entry point, HUD, mobile controls, and Three.js module loading.
- `index.html.backup`: Original game snapshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `git status --short`.
- Browser startup and page load succeeded; console had no errors. Four GPU `ReadPixels` performance warnings appeared during browser checks.
- `screenshots/title.png` was captured; interaction checks have not yet been run.

- Improve the retained hero’s procedural movement, turning, attacks, and jump animation.

## Requirements
- Preserve the original game and keep a backup.
- Use an orthographic isometric camera, camera-relative eight-direction movement, smooth acceleration/deceleration, collision, camera follow, and mobile-friendly touch controls.
- Keep code clean and mindful of mobile performance.
- Blend idle, walking, and running naturally; face the movement direction.
- Include takeoff, airborne, and landing animation phases.
- Retain the existing character; support Space and mobile jump input.
- Allow attacks to hit nearby enemies without requiring a forward-facing direction; each attack hits at most one target without shortening its animation.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js ES modules from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.180.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Keep the existing HTML HUD/gameplay structure where practical and retain the original in `index.html.backup`.
- Use procedural animation because the character has no skeletal rig.
- Use an analog mobile joystick with attack and jump controls.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented Three.js gameplay, UI integration, keyboard/touch controls, movement, collision, and camera follow.
- Added procedural hero pivots and idle, gait, turning, attack, and jump poses; connected animation to gameplay updates.
- Improved locomotion cadence based on travel distance, body lean and turn anticipation, takeoff/airborne/descent poses, landing compression, and attack wind-up/slash/follow-through.
- Added `attackHit` to prevent repeat hits during one attack; added mobile jump input and updated the controls hint.
- Confirmed title screen loads at `http://localhost:3002/`; WebGL2 context is available and browser console has no errors. Captured `screenshots/title.png`.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Verify gameplay interactions: movement, turning, attack animation and hit behavior, jump phases, and touch controls.
- Review final changes and validation results.

### Blocked
- Real Android device testing has not been performed; browser emulation cannot verify device-specific behavior.

## Next Move
1. Run browser interaction checks for movement, turning, attacks, jump transitions, and touch controls.
2. Recheck `node --check game.js`, `git diff --check`, and `git status`.
3. Test on Android if a device is available.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js gameplay, procedural hero animation, controls, jump state, collision, and camera follow.
- `index.html`: Entry point, HUD, mobile controls, and Three.js module loading.
- `index.html.backup`: Original game snapshot.
- `screenshots/title.png`: Captured title-screen screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed project files as untracked: `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `game.js`, `index.html`, `index.html.backup`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh`.
- Browser emitted four GPU `ReadPixels` performance warnings during checks; no console errors were reported.

## Objective
- Investigate why the game Preview appears unchanged after requested character-animation improvements, verify animation behavior in gameplay, and make any necessary targeted fix without rebuilding or redesigning the game.

## Requirements
- Preserve the existing game and backup.
- Verify saved changes, Preview-loaded files, and idle/walk/run animation playback in gameplay.
- Check for a character rig and usable animation clips; identify the exact cause of the unchanged appearance.
- Do not claim visible improvements unless verified in the running game.
- Report the exact cause and files changed.

## Decisions
- The character is procedurally built from Three.js meshes and pivots, not a rigged/skinned model; animation must be procedural unless the character asset changes.

## Work State
### Completed
- Confirmed `game.js` contains `createHeroModel()` and `animateHero()`, and the gameplay update loop calls `animateHero(dt, Math.hypot(hero.vx, hero.vy))`.
- Confirmed `index.html` loads `game.js` as a module.
- Confirmed Preview at `http://localhost:3002/` returns HTTP 200 and serves `game.js` containing `createHeroModel()`, `animateHero()`, and gait/animation state.
- Confirmed no `SkinnedMesh`, `AnimationMixer`, GLTF loader, or external character asset was found; the hero has no skeletal rig or imported animation clips.
- Existing browser checks exercised movement and action inputs but did not conclusively verify visibly distinct idle, walk, and run animation.
- Earlier `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Determine why Preview appears unchanged and conclusively verify hero poses during idle, walking, and running in the running game.
- Apply a focused animation fix only if verification shows improvements are missing or imperceptible.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Observe and capture idle, walking, and running gameplay frames in Preview; inspect hero pose/pivot changes.
2. Confirm Preview’s served `game.js` matches the current working file and isolate whether animation is not running, too subtle, or expected to be rigged/imported.
3. Make and verify a focused fix if needed; rerun syntax and diff checks.
4. Report the exact cause and changed files without claiming unverified visual improvements.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: procedural hero construction, animation logic, and gameplay update loop.
- `index.html`: Preview entry point loading `game.js`.
- `index.html.backup`: preserved original game.

## Important Context
- Project files are untracked (`game.js`, `index.html`, `index.html.backup`, and supporting files); no commit has been made.
- `animateHero()` uses movement/run blending and gait phase; visible idle/walk/run differences remain unverified.

input.prompt: Inspect game.js and index.html to identify why the game world looks platform-like and suggest minimal targeted changes to make it feel like a continuous natural world (not platformer), preserving existing gameplay. Report relevant functions and code areas; do not edit.

content.text:
<subagent sessionID="ses_e4b067891ffespS2aJURzAGe2v" state="completed">
## Why it reads as platform-like

The main cause is the ground construction in **`buildEnvironment()`** in `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js` (lines 115–149):

- Each region gets a flat rectangular floor, then an **InstancedMesh of 2.62-unit square boxes** on an 80-unit grid (lines 116–141). The boxes are separated by small regular gaps and stand noticeably above the base plane: their top is around `y = -0.028`, while the floor plane is at `y = -0.12`. That raised, gridded surface is the strongest “tiles/platforms” cue.
- Each region also gets a straight, uniform strip (lines 142–145). Its regular width and alignment make the ground read as a designed lane rather than terrain.
- Region-sized floor meshes and per-region palettes (lines 119–120) can make the world feel divided into large slabs at biome transitions.

`buildTreesAndRocks()` (lines 151–186) reinforces the sense of a corridor: trees are placed in two repeated rows near the map edges, and stone borders are placed at regular intervals along those same edges. The comment at line 178 explicitly describes the stones as borders for the traversable area.

The orthographic camera in `update()` (lines 799–804) gives the scene a board-game-like view, but it is a secondary factor. `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html` has no terrain markup; its vignette overlay (line 21) only affects framing.

## Minimal targeted changes to consider

1. **Flatten or remove the raised grid tiles** in `buildEnvironment()`. The smallest test is to lower their centers so their tops align with the base plane (currently the tile center is `-0.055`; aligning its top with the floor at `-0.12` would put the center near `-0.1475`). For a more natural look, replace the boxes with subtle, irregular ground-color variation rather than visible squares.
2. **Soften the path strip** in the same function: reduce its contrast/opacity, or break up its perfectly straight edges with a few irregular patches. Keep its placement if it helps navigation.
3. **Break the repeated edge pattern** in `buildTreesAndRocks()`: vary tree positions and spacing, and scatter some rocks or vegetation farther into the field. The collision limits in `blocked()` (lines 513–524) can stay unchanged—the visible scenery need not form a neat border.
4. If biome seams are conspicuous, soften the ground transition at the region boundaries rather than changing the region progression.

These changes are visual only. Movement, combat, pickups, gates, and level bounds use the existing world coordinates and collision logic, so they can be preserved.
</subagent>

I want to change the direction of this project significantly.

The current game world looks like a long floating platform with a character running across it. I no longer want this design.


IMPORTANT: You now have permission to completely redesign and replace the existing world environment. Do not preserve the old platform layout just for compatibility.


MY NEW WORLD DESIGN:


Create a spacious, natural, fully 3D fantasy adventure world with genuine isometric gameplay.


1. WORLD STRUCTURE


- Replace the long rectangular platform with a continuous natural landscape.
- Create large explorable areas rather than narrow running tracks.
- Use natural terrain with grass, hills, slopes, cliffs and valleys.
- Create winding paths, forests, rivers, bridges and caves.
- Add villages, ancient ruins, castles and hidden locations.
- Use natural environmental boundaries instead of floating platform edges.


2. EXPLORATION


- Allow the hero to move freely through the world.
- Create multiple connected areas with different elevations.
- Include secret paths, treasure locations and exploration opportunities.
- Make the environment feel like a real fantasy kingdom.


3. CAMERA


- Keep a genuine 3D orthographic isometric camera.
- Maintain the angled top-down adventure perspective.
- Do not turn the game into a side-scroller or endless runner.


4. WHAT TO PRESERVE


- Preserve the working player movement and joystick systems where possible.
- Preserve useful animation and combat code.
- Preserve the existing project structure where practical.
- You may rewrite or replace terrain, environment generation, world layout and level design.


5. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS


- Implement real 3D terrain and environmental geometry.
- Add appropriate collision detection and player navigation.
- Optimize rendering for Android.
- Ensure the world loads and runs correctly in Preview.


Do not create five small platforms or five linear boss arenas. Do not place a boss at the end of every narrow path.


The goal is a proper explorable 3D fantasy action-adventure RPG world, not a platform-running game.


Before implementation, briefly explain your redesign plan. Then implement it and verify it in Preview.
